policy.priority: Squared-magnitude interval span from producer/residual endpoints only; halve maximum threshold at each round.

scope: Two fresh real-model q8192/out512 processes use the same new whole DLL and otherwise identical retained stack, CLI, prompt and GB10 oracle. Every original output and callback ID and the first-logit tolerance0.125 are attached. The active owner replaces only30 linear OUT corrections with original algorithm0 production, original prepared K16 replay, bounded interval refinement and full residual/RMSNorm endpoint certification. The unchanged consumer executes afterward. The owner uses no external reference or completed control values. Counts and clocks describe actual execution, including producer, preparation, replay, conversion, completion and ownership. Certification remains conditional on the existing empirical producer envelope; observed failures disable skip certification and force complete original candidate replay. GB10 gates, not self-hashes or count identity, decide correctness. All30 intended linear layers execute the queued owner. Each token compacts candidates locally before one global allocation, while independent original K16 kernels consume the global count without a host count read. Packed BF16 interval endpoints reuse the F32 matrix storage, and the final conversion restores its rounded F32 carrier. Nineteen count clears, eighteen certificate launches and eighteen replay launches are bounded and ordered on the original stream. A single pair does not establish a repeatable speedup. No prefix, long-context, package or release qualification follows.

decision.decision: Keep variant2 default-off and outside the retained stack. All intended layers and GB10 boundaries pass, with no observed interval failure. The single 677.8043ms TTFT reduction does not establish a repeatable gain or meet the10000ms product gate. Preserve this qualified experiment for later combined structural trials; do not infer speedup from candidate counts alone.
